joined this GP in September on the recommendation of a senior NHS manager. Since then, I have been unexpectedly removed from their care, leaving me in a very difficult position with my health.

My repeat prescriptions were removed without informing me or my consultants. This forced me to use the triage system daily, often in severe pain, but I was again only able to contact physiotherapists or was ignored. My health deteriorated, and I was denied medication, being redirected to mental health services instead. I ended up in A&E, where my spinal injury was found to be worsening and now requires surgery.

After this, the GP refused further pain medication, citing incorrect records about my prescription collection. Despite me and Boots pharmacy providing evidence, I was unable to get the medication I needed, resulting in frequent A&E visits. Only two days’ worth would be prescribed at a time, with long waits for more and no explanation. They refused to inform my consultant, and nerve pain medication prescribed by my consultant was also refused, leaving me in severe pain.

Referrals and Records

A blood test in November indicated serious health issues. The doctor made referrals but omitted key information, resulting in refusal. Attempts to correct this were met with misleading responses and no action. I was eventually told I might have ovarian failure, but no referral was made, and incorrect diagnoses were sent across NHS services.

Referrals focused on incorrect diagnoses, despite repeated requests for correction. I had to request a right to restrict on my file, but was misled about its implementation, which affected my safeguarding and ability to get medication from urgent care.

I am currently waiting for results regarding possible cancer and neurosurgery but was removed from the GP’s care in the same week I was in hospital. This has been the worst week of my life.

My requests for support and communication were ignored. As a deaf and neurodivergent patient, I asked for help with forms after receiving threats, but received none. Even a senior NHS manager who supported me was ignored.

I was wrongly accused of submitting over 250 triages in 30 days, which I dispute, and was refused an explanation or evidence. The reason given to the NHS was my difficulty attending face-to-face appointments, even though I attended the only one offered and the clinic is next to my office and this never being mentioned to me.

I asked the surgery to communicate with my consultants about medication refusal, hoping for a private prescription, but this was not done.

Escalation and Removal

I was threatened with removal if I submitted more triages, but my declining health forced me to continue seeking help. I am glad I did, as it led to a cancer-screening referral and recognition of my spinal relapse, which had not been believed by the GP and I could not get my medication.

My requests to speak to the practice manager and named GP were refused. I noticed records being deleted by a third party, with no explanation given, and requests to correct errors in my file were also refused.

After removal, I received calls from GPs to provide medication and referrals—actions that should have happened months earlier. It appears my file is being tidied before my removal in two weeks.
